instana_analysis_guide.overview:
Comprehensive guide for using Instana MCP server tools to gather observability data, analyze application performance, and identify anomalies. This guide covers all available Instana resources and their optimal usage patterns for incident investigation.
CRITICAL: Instana is the PRIMARY source for ALL metrics, services, and application data. - When asked for metrics: Use Instana MCP tools - When asked for services: Use Instana MCP tools (manage_applications) - When asked for application data: Use Instana MCP tools - When asked for infrastructure metrics: Use Instana MCP tools (analyze_infrastructure)
OpenShift commands should ONLY be used during root cause analysis to correlate cluster state with Instana findings.

tool.name: manage_events
tool.description: Access Instana events including issues, incidents, changes, and Kubernetes info events

operation.name: get_issues
operation.purpose: Retrieve issue events (problems detected by Instana)

parameters.param: Show only events with state changes (boolean)

operation.name: get_incidents
operation.purpose: Retrieve incident events (grouped issues requiring attention)
operation.when_to_use: When investigating active or recent incidents that have been escalated

operation.name: get_kubernetes_info_events
operation.purpose: Get Kubernetes-specific events with detailed analysis
operation.when_to_use: When investigating pod lifecycle issues, scheduling problems, or K8s-specific errors

operation.name: get_agent_monitoring_events
operation.purpose: Get agent monitoring events (agent health, connectivity)
operation.when_to_use: When suspecting agent issues or gaps in monitoring coverage

operation.name: get_changes
operation.when_to_use: To correlate incidents with recent changes or deployments

operation.name: get_event
operation.purpose: Get detailed information about a specific event

parameters.param: The specific event ID to retrieve

tool.name: analyze_infrastructure
tool.description: Two-pass infrastructure analysis for querying entity metrics (JVM, Kubernetes, hosts, databases)

pass.title: Intent to Schema
pass.description: Provide natural language intent and entity hint. Server returns full schema with available metrics and filters.
pass.example: <use_mcp_tool> <server_name>instana</server_name> <tool_name>analyze_infrastructure</tool_name> <arguments> { "intent": "maximum heap size of JVM on host galactica1", "entity": "jvm" } </arguments> </use_mcp_tool>

pass.title: Selections to Results
pass.description: Provide exact selections from schema. Server builds payload and calls API.

parameters.param: Array of tag names to group by (optional)

pattern.name: incident_timeline_reconstruction
pattern.description: Reconstruct the sequence of events leading to an incident

steps.step: Get incidents and issues for the time window
Get change events to identify recent deployments
Get Kubernetes events for infrastructure changes
Correlate timestamps to build timeline

pattern.name: service_dependency_analysis
pattern.description: Understand service call patterns and dependencies

steps.step: List all services in the application
Query metrics for each service (calls, errors, latency)
Identify services with elevated error rates
Trace upstream and downstream dependencies

pattern.name: performance_degradation_analysis
pattern.description: Investigate latency increases or throughput drops

steps.step: Get latency percentiles (P50, P90, P95, P99) over time
Compare current metrics to baseline
Identify slow endpoints or services
Check infrastructure metrics (CPU, memory, GC)
Look for resource saturation or contention

pattern.name: error_spike_investigation
pattern.description: Investigate sudden increases in error rates

steps.step: Get error count and rate metrics
Group errors by type or endpoint
Check for recent changes or deployments
Examine traces for failed requests
Look for downstream service failures
Query JVM heap usage and GC metrics
Check container CPU and memory utilization
Examine database connection pool metrics
Look for thread pool exhaustion
Check for disk space or I/O saturation

practice.title: Start with broad queries, then narrow down
practice.description: Begin with application-level metrics to identify affected services, then drill down to specific endpoints or infrastructure components

practice.title: Use appropriate time windows
practice.description: - For active incidents: last 1-6 hours - For post-incident analysis: 24-48 hours - For trend analysis: 7-30 days

practice.title: Correlate multiple data sources
practice.description: Don't rely on a single metric. Cross-reference: - Error rates with latency - Application metrics with infrastructure metrics - Instana events with deployment changes

practice.title: Use filters effectively
practice.description: Apply tag filters to focus on specific: - Applications or services - Environments (prod, staging) - Regions or availability zones - Specific hosts or pods

practice.title: Leverage grouping for aggregation
practice.description: Group metrics by relevant dimensions: - service.name for service-level analysis - endpoint.name for endpoint-level analysis - host.name for infrastructure analysis - kubernetes.namespace.name for namespace analysis

practice.title: Check SLO compliance
practice.description: If SLOs are configured, check error budget status to understand the severity and business impact of the incident

possible_causes.cause: Incorrect time range (too narrow or in the future)
Wrong tag filter (typo in service/application name)
Entity type doesn't exist in environment

solutions.solution: Verify time range is in the past and covers incident window
Use catalog operations to get valid tag names
Check entity type spelling against schema
Narrow time window to incident timeframe
Apply tag filters to focus on affected components
Use max_events parameter to limit results

possible_causes.cause: Metric not collected for this entity type
Agent not configured to collect metric

solutions.solution: Use get_metric_catalog to see available metrics
Check entity type supports the metric
